**Fixes a restart that installed the update onto a copy you were not running, and gives
macOS real updates instead of a link.**

## *Restart and update* appeared to do nothing

On Windows the installer replaces one specific folder: the one recorded when the app was
installed. That is the right thing for it to do, and it is why nobody noticed that the app
never checked whether the copy asking for the update was that folder.

If it was not — a build run straight out of `release/win-unpacked`, a copy moved somewhere
else, a shortcut left pointing at an old location — pressing **Restart and update**
worked perfectly and changed nothing you could see. The installer ran. It installed. It
replaced a copy that was not the one on screen, and then started that copy, which found
the original still running and quit again on the spot, exactly as a second instance
should. The widget in front of you was untouched, still on the old version, still starting
at login, still finding the same release six hours later and offering the same restart.
Nothing said any of this had happened.

It says so now, before offering anything: a copy that is not the installed one reports
that plainly and offers the download page instead of a button that cannot work.

Pressing the button has also stopped being silent. **About** shows *Restarting to finish
the update…* while it happens, and if the quit is refused — this widget lives in the tray,
suppresses the ordinary quit and holds a window parented to the taskbar, all of which can
leave `app.quit()` asking politely and getting nowhere — it is taken after six seconds
rather than left to an installer waiting on a process that never goes. If the installer
never starts at all, that is now an error on the card with the reason in it.

## macOS updates itself now

Since 1.2.1 a Mac copy would tell you a new version existed and hand you the downloads
page, because Squirrel — the thing that installs macOS updates — will only swap in a build
whose code signature satisfies the running app's, and this project has no Apple Developer
ID to sign with.

So Squirrel is out of it. The app now fetches the `.dmg` for its own architecture, checks
it against the SHA-512 the release publishes — the only thing standing where a signature
would normally stand — mounts it, and replaces the bundle it is running from. **Download
updates automatically** works on a Mac again, the notification and the menus offer a
restart rather than a link, and the quarantine flag is cleared on the way past, so there
is no `xattr` command to run after an update.

The copy is made beside the old bundle before anything is moved, and the old one only
leaves once the new one is in place; if any step fails the previous version goes back
exactly where it was. Either way the app is started again at the end. A failed update
should cost you a version, not your widget.

A Mac copy that *cannot* be replaced — running from inside a mounted `.dmg`, or from a
managed `/Applications` — still says so and offers the page, as before.

## No second copies, on either platform

This was already true on Windows and is worth stating: the installer uninstalls the
previous version before writing the new one, so an update replaces an install rather than
adding one beside it. On macOS the swap now does the same thing by construction — the old
bundle is deleted once the new one is in place, rather than left for you to find later.

## A log to read when it goes wrong

Everything the updater does is written to `updater.log`, beside the settings file:

| Platform | Path                                                          |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows  | `%APPDATA%\claude-usage-widget\updater.log`                    |
| macOS    | `~/Library/Application Support/claude-usage-widget/updater.log` |

electron-updater logs to the console by default, and a packaged Windows app has no console
to log to — which is why the original failure left nothing behind to read.

## Downloads

| Platform              | File                           |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Windows 10 / 11       | `Claude-Usage-Setup-1.2.2.exe` |
| macOS — Apple silicon | `Claude-Usage-1.2.2-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS — Intel         | `Claude-Usage-1.2.2-x64.dmg`   |

macOS refuses the first launch of an unsigned download — *"Claude Usage is damaged and
can't be opened"*. It is not damaged; that is the quarantine flag, and clearing it is one
command:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Claude Usage.app"
```

From this version on that is a first-install chore only. Updates clear it themselves.
